candidate.title: Nextera Rapid Capture
candidate.scope: The single Nextera Rapid Capture target-enrichment schematic, beginning with already denatured and pooled Nextera library fragments, proceeding through biotinylated-probe hybridization, magnetic bead capture and elution, and ending at a library product ready for cluster generation. The biological target is a sequence region within the library insert, and the retained target-bearing library fragment is the prospective sequencing substrate. No alternative method, upstream Nextera library construction, separate pooling/denaturation operation, sequencing operation or primary-paper implementation is specified. All chemistry and applicability claims are limited to this depiction.

states.label: Denatured and pooled fragments from Nextera library
features: Input library is already denatured and pooled; these preparative actions are not separately drawn.
Multiple variable-length fragments are represented by single lines; one highlighted fragment contains a labeled Target region.
Colored flanking library segments are present before capture; their P5/P7 and Index 2/Index 1 labels are provided on the final product.

This is a library-material endpoint; cluster generation, sequencing reads and data analysis are not depicted.

operations.label: Hybridize probes to targets
operations.description: The already denatured, pooled Nextera library is combined with biotinylated target probe, as indicated by the plus sign and downward arrow. The output is a library fragment with the short probe hybridized at its target region; the fragment retains its flanking library segments.
operations.mechanism: Target-directed probe hybridization, explicitly labeled in the diagram; no enzyme-mediated conversion or synthesis is shown.
operations.information_effect: Associates the target region of a library fragment with a biotin-bearing capture probe. The original library fragment remains the target-sequence carrier.

operations.label: Capture on magnetic beads
operations.description: The downward route carries the probe-target hybrid to magnetic bead capture material. The output retains the target-bearing library fragment through its probe-associated attachment to the bead surface.
operations.mechanism: The drawing places the biotin-bearing part of the hybrid at the bead surface, supporting probe-mediated immobilization. It does not name the bead-surface binding chemistry.
operations.information_effect: Provides physical retention of probe-associated library fragments from the input pool. This supports intended target enrichment, but the drawing establishes neither perfect target specificity nor capture efficiency.

evidence.rationale: The short probe remains hybridized to the long fragment, and its biotin-associated symbol is drawn at the bead surface; this supports an attachment route through the probe without identifying the surface receptor.

operations.label: Elute
operations.description: Elution changes the bead-associated target-bearing library into a free library product, depicted without the bead or short capture probe and labeled ready for cluster generation. The final target region retains the flanking library features.
operations.mechanism: Release from the bead-associated capture complex is depicted; the chemical mechanism of release is not specified.
operations.information_effect: The readout carrier available for subsequent sequencing is the retained library insert, with Target between Index 2 and Index 1 and P5/P7 outside them. Thus downstream reads can describe captured library target sequence; the diagram does not depict sequencing, quantify enrichment or establish complete target coverage.
